1.s: Paul thanks God for the Philippians’ partnership. His imprisonment has advanced the gospel. “For to me to live is Christ, and to die is gain.”
1.d: “He who began a good work in you will complete it.”

2.s: Have the mind of Christ, who “emptied himself, taking the form of a servant”, humbled himself to death on a cross, and was highly exalted, “that at the name of Jesus every knee should bow.”
2.d: The Christ hymn (2:6–11) is central to Christian teaching about the incarnation. Timothy and Epaphroditus are commended.

3.s: Paul counts all his credentials as loss “for the excellency of the knowledge of Christ Jesus”. “I press on toward the goal.”
3.d: Paul lists his Jewish pedigree, then sets it aside.

4.s: “Rejoice in the Lord always!” “In nothing be anxious, but in everything, by prayer and petition with thanksgiving, let your requests be made known to God,” and his peace will guard your hearts. “I can do all things through Christ.”
4.d: Paul has learned contentment in plenty and in want. Think about whatever is true, honourable, just, pure and lovely.
